newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares little changed in mixed trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares little changed in mixed trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed almost unchanged on Wednesday in mixed trading as the market continued expressing concern over the political situation, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares fell 0.03 percent, or 0.07 points, to 252.72 on all-share turnover of 146 million shekels against 137 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.09 percent lower at 261.48.

"The fact that the market closed unchanged today is meaningless because it was the outcome of heavy trading by options speculators. If it weren't for Teva we would have seen a sharp drop," said Idan Azoulay at Impact Union Protfoliio Management.
Elisha Rosenfeld of Lehava Investments added that foreign investors were active buying shares, preventing the market from falling.

Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, the volume leader, surged 5.75 percent to 20,541 agorot on volume of 15 million shekels. Teva's Nasdaq-traded American depositary receipts ADRs) rose 4.1 percent on Tuesday after several American investment banks issued buy recommendations for the share.
"There is much uncertainty in the market because of the Bar-On story and the Har Homa building. Investors are sitting on the fence waiting for further developments," Azoulay said.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and other officials in his government are being questioned by police in connection with charges that the short-lived appointment of Roni Bar-On as attorney-general was part of a deal for a plea bargain in the corruption trial of Aryeh Deri, a key figure in the governing coalition.
Meanwhile, a ministerial committee was scheduled to convene later on Wednesday to approve a plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews on Har Homa, a Jerusalem hill taken by Israel in the 1967 war.

Palestinians and Israeli leftists have warned the plan could ignite Arab rage reminiscent of September clashes sparked by Netanyahu's opening of an entrance to a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.
"The market is very nervous," Rosenfeld said. "I think all the political events are only an excuse for investors to take profits."
Traders said that as long as the political uncertainty remains, the market will be volatile with a downside tendency.

Other active shares included Israel Chemicals, which fell 3.0 percent to 368 agorot on turnover of 5.9 million shekels, and Bank Leumi, which rose 2.0 percent to 560 agorot on volume of 5.6 million shekels.
